**No.** The excerpt (the opening of Stefan Zweig's *Der Amokläufer*) uses a conventional frame-narrative structure. A first-person narrator looks back years later, briefly mentions a mysterious incident in Naples, and then, after a section break, returns chronologically to the beginning of the voyage in Calcutta.

This retrospective framing does introduce a mild non-linearity, since the outcome is hinted at before the backstory. But it was a standard, well-established device of the novella form, especially in early 20th-century German-language fiction. The prose is richly descriptive, yet the format, voice, plot structure and genre are all traditional. Nothing about the shape or organization of the story is unusual or inventive.
